details: For every finite binary class with $\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)\geq1$, $\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)\leq2\,\mathrm E(\mathcal H)-3$; equivalently $\mathrm E(\mathcal H)\geq(\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)+3)/2$.
proof: First quotient coordinates having the same evaluation vector on $\mathcal H$; the resulting domain has $\mathrm E(\mathcal H)$ points and preserves spherical dimension. The antipodal realizable-distribution complex is a finite subcomplex of the realizable-distribution complex and therefore has dimension at most $\mathrm E(\mathcal H)-1$. The local Borsuk--Ulam theorem in the cited paper forbids an antipodality-preserving map from $S^d$ whenever $2(\mathrm E-1)\leq d$. Hence $d\leq2\mathrm E-3$ for every admitted $d\geq1$.
name: Effective Range / Spherical Dimension (affine)
